{{short description|Expresses a Gauss sum using a product of values of the p-adic gamma function}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Gross–Koblitz formula''', introduced by {{harvs|txt|last1=Gross|author1-link=Benedict Gross|last2=Koblitz|author2-link=Neal Koblitz|year=1979}} expresses a [[Gauss sum]] using a product of values of the [[p-adic gamma function|''p''-adic gamma function]]. It is an analog of the [[Chowla–Selberg formula]] for the usual [[gamma function]]. It implies the [[Hasse–Davenport relation]] and generalizes the [[Stickelberger theorem]].
{{harvtxt|Boyarsky|1980}} gave another proof of the Gross–Koblitz formula ("Boyarsky" being a pseudonym of [[Bernard Dwork]]), and 
{{harvtxt|Robert|2001}} gave an elementary proof.

==Statement==

The Gross–Koblitz formula states that the Gauss sum <math>\tau</math> can be given in terms of the <math>p</math>-adic gamma function <math>\Gamma_p</math> by

:<math>\tau_q(r) = -\pi^{s_p(r)}\prod_{0\leq i <f}\Gamma_p\!\left(\frac{r^{(i)}}{q-1} \right)</math>

where
* <math>q</math> is a power <math>p^f</math> of a prime <math>p</math>,
* <math>r</math> is an integer with <math>0 \leq r < q-1</math>,
* <math>r^{(i)}</math> is the integer whose base-<math>p</math> expansion is a cyclic permutation of the <math>f</math> digits of <math>r</math> by <math>i</math> positions,
* <math>s_p(r)</math> is the sum of the base-<math>p</math> digits of <math>r</math>,
* <math>\tau_q(r) = \sum_{a^{q-1}=1} a^{-r} \zeta_\pi^{\text{Tr}(a)}</math>, where the sum is over roots of unity in the extension <math>\mathbb{Q}_p(\pi)</math>,
* <math>\pi</math> satisfies <math>\pi^{p - 1} = -p</math>, and
* <math>\zeta_\pi</math> is the <math>p</math>th root of unity congruent to <math>1 + \pi</math> modulo <math>\pi^2</math>.
